newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday May 9.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Trade union federation leader Sergio Cofferati harshly criticised prime minister Romano Prodi's comments on making cuts to pensions' spending in a television programme Tuesday night. Cofferati said pensions should be talked about first with trade unions (all).
* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimio D'Alema said he favoured the direct election of a prime minister, thus meeting the approval of centre-right opposition (all).
* Cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli said the 1998 budget would not be brought forward (all).

* Giuliano Amato, chairman of Italy's antitrust authority, said the authority will complete an inquiry into the country's financial services sector by November. Amato also said government delays in approving rules for frequency band access are seriously prejudicing potential users of DECT advanced cordless telephone system. He also confirmed his intention to resign as chairman of the authority before the year end (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed retail sales of medium and large firms in Italy rose 1.6 percent in January 1997 compared with a year earlier. Istat figures were calculated on a new base of 1995=100 (Sole 24 Ore).
* The Finance Ministry said Italy's tax revenues rose seven percent in 1996 to 519.7 trillion lire from 486.7 trillion in 1995 (all).

* Roberto Colaninno, chief executive of information technology group Olivetti said the company was looking for strong allies. Colaninno added the group would not make a capital increase at least for this year (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the government was going ahead with its vast programme of privatisations adding the role of industrial state holding IRI should be considered as finished (all). Ciampi is reportedly studying a 1998 budget for 24 trillion lire (La Repubblica).
* State-controlled energy group Eni's exploration and production arm Agip said its consolidated profit rose 33 percent in 1996 to 2.74 trillion lire compared with 2.06 trillion in 1995 (Sole 24 Ore).
* Franco Tato, managing director of Italian electricity group Enel, said he expected 1996 results to be in line with the previous year when it had a net profit of 1.15 trillion lire (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
